title: SOFR Rate Observation - April 15, 2026

source.name: FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)

summary: The Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) closed at 3.72% on April 15, 2026, up 6 basis points from the prior day's reading of 3.66%. The rate has trended higher over the past five business days, rising from 3.57% on April 9 to the current level.
key_points: SOFR closed at 3.72% on 2026-04-15, up 6 bps from 3.66% on 2026-04-14
Total increase over the observation period: +15 bps
No explanatory context provided for the rate movement in this data snapshot
Source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis FRED database
why_it_matters: SOFR is the primary benchmark reference rate for overnight Treasury-backed repurchase agreements and serves as the reference rate for an estimated $20+ trillion in loans, derivatives, and financial contracts. Movements in SOFR signal changes in short-term collateralized funding conditions and can indicate stress or tightness in the repo market plumbing.
macro_context: SOFR movements reflect short-term funding conditions but this snapshot provides no explanatory context for the rate trend. The rising SOFR over this period could reflect seasonal liquidity dynamics, Treasury settlement flows, or broader money market conditions.
market_structure_context: SOFR is calculated by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York as the median rate on tri-party repo transactions collateralized by Treasury and agency securities. This daily snapshot captures end-of-day overnight funding costs in the Treasury repo market, which is critical market infrastructure for collateral mobility and short-term liquidity management.
